notes: Stored edit chosen for relation coverage (CRITERIA Rule 12), migrated from the earlier record (same edit). Derivability very_unlikely: 'Austin is the capital of Texas' is stated about a thousand times verbatim and follows from no other fact. The edit moves a city between countries, so it is the topic's subproperty (related near: capital_of is a subproperty of located_in) and role-chain (related far: capital_of composed with located_in) record. In every world Ciudad Juárez lies in Texas and no longer in Chihuahua or Mexico, because a city lies in only one state and one country (revision facts, each with a check). Earlier audit flags handled: the old check 'Ciudad Juárez lies in only one country' (answer 'no', missed by 3 models) was a misstated premise; it is replaced by the plain definitional checks 'a city lies in only one state/country'. The Chinese question now names the United States (two models missed the old wording). Derived[0] (binding) uses the inverse and subproperty steps, so it is labelled subproperty with via capital_of. Related near and far also rely on the definitional revision fact that a city lies in only one state or country; the two definitional checks replace the old 'only one country' check but have not been re-audited. The Chinese question names the United States but its audit (two models missed the old wording) has not been re-run: if two or more still miss it, drop or simplify it. Evidence: Houston in Texas has counts above 100; derived facts have near-zero direct-form counts beside common premises. Wikipedia (429) refused further requests, so the Rio Grande and Houston bridges have no new quotes (Ciudad Juárez quotes are earlier ones). related[1]: functional, the original fact from the city's side. related (2026-11-14, one related question): the county seat of Travis County is the capital of Texas, stored whole (Wikipedia: 'Its county seat and most populous city is Austin, the state's capital'); replaces the Colorado River question, whose sentence had no whole quote or count.
